class.name: CgameFLIPFluid
class.brief_description: 2D FLIP/PIC fluid on a staggered grid with destructible walls and a moving circle obstacle.
class.description: [CgameFLIPFluid] is a 2D water solver that blends the PIC and FLIP methods (Zhu and Bridson, 2005) on a MAC grid (Harlow and Welch, 1965). Each step integrates particles, pushes overlapping particles apart, transfers velocities to the grid with bilinear weights, projects the grid velocity to be divergence free with over-relaxed Gauss-Seidel sweeps (with optional density-based drift compensation), and transfers the result back with a PIC/FLIP blend. The step structure follows Matthias Müller's Ten Minute Physics tutorial 18 (MIT license). The domain is [member cols] by [member rows] square cells of size [member cell_size]; the outer border is always solid. Individual cells can be made solid or opened again with [method set_solid] (for example a breakable dam), and one circular obstacle can move through the fluid. Coordinates are y-up. Particle collision and the grid-to-particle transfer run on the [WorkerThreadPool] with per-particle ownership of the written data, so results are deterministic. Gauss-Seidel pressure solving, particle-to-grid scattering and push-apart are order dependent and run serially. This class is the native counterpart of the GDScript [code]flip_fluid.gd[/code] and exposes the same API. [codeblock] var sim := CgameFLIPFluid.new() sim.setup(30, 12, 0.1) sim.add_water_block(Vector2(0.2, 0.2), Vector2(1.3, 0.9)) func _physics_process(delta): sim.step(delta) [/codeblock]

method.name: add_water_block
method.description: Fills the box from [param lo] to [param hi] with a hexagonal lattice of particles, skipping wall cells. Returns the number of particles added.

method.name: average_height
method.description: Returns the mean particle y position, or [code]0.0[/code] if there are no particles.

method.name: cell_of
method.description: Returns the grid cell containing [param position], clamped to the grid.

method.name: cell_type_at
method.description: Returns the [enum CellType] of [param cell] as classified after the last step. Cells outside the grid are [constant CELL_SOLID].

method.name: clear_particles
method.description: Removes all particles. Walls and the obstacle are kept.

method.name: divergence_max
method.description: Returns the largest absolute divergence of the current grid velocity over fluid cells.

method.name: get_cell_density
method.description: Returns the particle density per cell from the last step. The index of cell [code](i, j)[/code] is [code]i * rows + j[/code].

method.name: get_cell_types
method.description: Returns the [enum CellType] of every cell. The index of cell [code](i, j)[/code] is [code]i * rows + j[/code].

method.name: is_wall
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if [param cell] is a wall. Cells outside the grid count as walls.

method.name: kinetic_energy
method.description: Returns the summed kinetic energy of all particles per unit mass.

method.name: particle_positions
method.description: Returns a copy of all particle positions.

method.name: particle_velocities
method.description: Returns a copy of all particle velocities.

method.name: set_obstacle
method.description: Places a circular obstacle that moves with [param velocity] every step and also acts as a particle collider.

method.name: set_solid
method.description: Turns [param cell] into a wall or opens it again (destructible barrier). The outer border cannot be changed.

method.name: setup
method.description: Resets the simulation to an empty domain of [param cols] by [param rows] cells (each at least 4) of size [param cell_size]. Removes all particles and the obstacle and rebuilds the border walls.

method.name: step
method.description: Advances the simulation by [param dt] seconds. Does nothing if [param dt] is not positive or there are no particles.

members.member: Edge length of a grid cell. Set through [method setup].
Number of grid columns. Set through [method setup].
If [code]true[/code], over-dense cells are decompressed during the pressure solve to keep the particle volume from drifting.
Blend between PIC ([code]0[/code], stable and viscous) and FLIP ([code]1[/code], lively and noisy).
Nominal fluid density. Kept for API compatibility; the solver works with relative particle density.
The largest absolute divergence measured at the start of the last pressure solve, before projection.
[code]true[/code] if an obstacle was placed with [method set_obstacle].
Over-relaxation factor of the Gauss-Seidel pressure solve. Values between [code]1[/code] and [code]2[/code] converge faster.
Collision radius of a particle. Defaults to [code]0.3 * cell_size[/code].
Number of Gauss-Seidel sweeps per step.
Number of particle push-apart passes per step.
Number of grid rows. Set through [method setup].

constants.constant: The cell is open and contains no particles.
The cell is a wall or covered by the obstacle.
